Our Facilities
Glebelands School is fortunate to be located in expansive grounds nestled beneath the Surrey Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. We have a range of facilities available for public hire including our brand new 3G football pitch, outdoor areas, sports facilities and our main hall for large functions. Please click here to see our facilities page.

Computer Science
Students studying Computer Science at Glebelands are taught a broad range of topics across their school journey.
Units include computer game building, web development, spreadsheets, coding and computer science theory. We feel it is important that students learn a broad range of skills and knowledge that they can use throughout school and later life.

Drama
Through Drama, students are continually developing practical, relevant and transferable life skills that will help them secure a job in the future and be successful in any career they choose.
The practical elements of the course enable students to develop their dramatic and performance skills and prepare them well should they wish to continue their training in the Performing Arts. There are many careers in the Arts which the Drama course will complement and not just in performance. There are many unseen backstage roles such as director, producer, designers in lighting, costume, sound effects, stage make-up.

Maths
The Mathematics Department at Glebelands forms a key part of the core curriculum offer. Students will continue to develop the mathematics and numeracy that they have learnt at primary school.
The aim of mathematics is to improve students’ numerical skills to enable them to progress to further studies in mathematics or other related subjects. It is particularly important for careers in the Science, Technology and Engineering, Finance, Economics and the Social Sciences. It also prepares students who go directly into employment to have a functional level of mathematical skills.
The course has been designed to encourage students to:
Consolidate basic mathematical skills
Apply knowledge and understanding to solve problems

Science
The Science Department aims to provide a broad and balanced Science education for all. This encompasses and promotes progression, continuity and access to Science for all students.
We provide, through well-constructed studies of investigative and practical activities, a Science education which enables the learner to understand how Science operates, to be able to be scientific in analysing and solving problems and appreciate Science as a human activity.
Our primary aim is to ensure that all students gain knowledge and understanding of Science and that they reach their true potential in this subject. This can only be achieved by strategic planning, monitoring, evaluation of procedures, effective and diverse teaching and learning in classrooms and the whole school environment.
Science Brochure

Art
The Art department offers a first rate exciting and aspirational Art education.
We aspire to build strong foundations of Art skills and knowledge which can then be formulated into exciting experiments and investigations into Art. We hope to facilitate all creative learners, broaden imaginations and inspire self-expression through our culturally diverse, practical focused and knowledge rich Art curriculum.

English
In the English department at Glebelands we aim to encourage students to become independent, creative learners who use their imagination and express their own opinions with confidence.
We think that these skills are vital and will support them no matter what they decide to do, both in school and beyond. We also hope to foster in our students a love of reading and of the spoken and written word and ensure we introduce them to authors from a range of diverse backgrounds and cultures.

Geography
Our aim within Geography at Glebelands is to enable students to understand and thrive in the ever-changing world in which we live.
Geography inspires students to become good citizens by exploring their unique place in the world, their values and their responsibilities to other people and the environment.
Geography Brochure

History
The purpose and intent of studying history at Glebelands School is to share with students the complex dynamics of past societies and cultures.
We frame our learning in class through the lens of historical enquiry, delving into a variety of sources to explore the past. We aim to foster in our students a curiosity for the world around them that will remain with them for the rest of their lives. Our curriculum has been designed specifically to develop students’ curiosity, knowledge, sense of identity and understand their place in the world. Through the course of study students will gain a deep understanding of how and why the world has changed and developed over time.

Modern Foreign Languages
The intent of the Modern Foreign Language department is to enable students to develop all four skills necessary to become a successful linguist. This enables them to use French or Spanish in their future; whether that be in a career or whilst travelling.
We are passionate about broadening students’ horizons and preparing them for higher education and the world of work through a positive learning experience of both the language itself and the cultures behind the language. We seek to ensure that all our students acquire both the knowledge and cultural capital which they are both entitled to and need to succeed.

PE
The overall intent of Physical Education at Glebelands is to enjoy being physically active and develop movement skills in a range of activities.
We want our students to develop their physical literacy, the confidence to learn and refine physical skills, apply these in different activities and contexts and to be able to develop social, emotional and cognitive skills through PE lessons.

Learning Partners Academy Trust
Glebelands School is a member of the Learning Partners Academy Trust, based in the South of England. The trust brings schools together so that they can thrive and enable their pupils to become the best they can be. As indicated in the name, Learning Partners wholeheartedly embraces the educational qualities of both learning and partnership. Its mission is to create a love of learning in the lives of pupils, and to encourage partnership and collaboration because we achieve more when we work together.
Across the trust, we are guided by the following values in all that we do:
We will always strive for excellence – in every school, for every child.
We will collaborate and work in partnership with others to improve outcomes for all.
Learning that Inspires
We will enable everyone to access inspirational and thoughtful learning, stretching their horizons.
We will restlessly pursue creative and innovative ways of enriching the education of all children.
We will be open, transparent and make decisions fairly.
You can find out more about the Trust Vison, Mission and Values here.
Please visit the trust's homepage: learningpartners.org

Design & Technology
Creativity, celebrating ideas and innovation is at the heart of Design and Technology at Glebelands.
Sustainable, explorative and creative user centric design that incorporates new materials, industry-based CAD software and manufacturing techniques incorporating CAM is in the DNA of how we teach. Students learn how to research, generate ideas, problem solve and bring to life great ideas from paper to practical outcomes.

Open Evening & Daytime Tours
Our Open Evening for prospective September 2027 students will be on Thursday 24th September 2026. We also hold morning tours in the weeks after the Open Evening to show you what makes Glebelands special. Booking is required for morning tours and these tours start at 9am promptly. Please email info@glebelands.surrey.sch.uk or phone 01483 542400 to book your place on the morning tours.
Information about our educational offer can be found in our Prospectus and Exam Results. You can also see our Virtual Tour of the school here.
If you are thinking of applying to Glebelands School for your son or daughter at other points in the year and would like to see the school in action, please contact reception on 01483 542400 or email info@glebelands.surrey.sch.uk. Information on admissions can be found here. We look forward to welcoming you.

RE
Religious Studies at Glebelands provides an intellectually grounded, philosophically and theologically astute exploration of ultimate questions of meaning, purpose and truth that have direct relevance to British society.
We live in a world where politics, culture and religion are often fused together. Our aim is to cultivate religious literacy, so that our students can address the problems, challenges and opportunities they encounter in the world in an attentive, reasonable and responsible manner.
Under the Education Act 1996, parents have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education (RE) lessons without providing a reason. If you wish to exercise this right, please submit a written request to the Headteacher via info@glebelands.surrey.sch.uk.
